one_liner: Research C++ RRR-style H0-compressed bitvectors with faster block decoding; beat SDSL rrr_vector on access at block size 63.
what_it_does: Static compressed bitvectors that store each block as a (class = popcount, offset) pair, as in SDSL's rrr_vector, but with different block decoders and code assignments: recursive (h0_bv.hpp), iterative 8-bit-chunk decoding for b=63/64 (h0_63.hpp, h0_it.hpp), a sparsified lookup table for b=15/24 (h0_gap.hpp), and generated weighted de Bruijn code tables (weightedDeBrujin.py). Each class is constructed from an sdsl::bit_vector and exposes access(i), rank(i), select(s) and size accessors; it does not implement SDSL's rank_support/select_support or serialize/load interfaces, so it is not a drop-in rrr_vector replacement. Hybrid bitvector experiments (hyb_*.hpp) are patched copies of SDSL's hyb_vector.
how_it_is_fast: RRR decoding of a block offset into its bit pattern dominates query time at large block sizes. h0_63/h0_it decode a 63/64-bit block iteratively in 8-bit chunks using compile-time binomial and limit tables (constexpr std::array), so a block is decoded with a few table lookups instead of SDSL's bit-by-bit combinatorial walk. h0_gap stores a sampled (gap) lookup table of all block codes for b<32, and the de Bruijn variants assign non-lexicographic codes to blocks (the SEA 2025 paper 'Succinct Rank Dictionaries Revisited' argues these can give faster queries). Select uses BMI2 _pdep_u64 for the in-word step.
when_to_use: Research or prototyping of RRR-style compressed bitvectors for FM-indexes and wavelet trees, where you want SDSL rrr_vector<63> space (about 0.71 bits/bit on WT-DNA-1GB, same as SDSL) with lower access latency (249 vs 345 ns in the notebook).

Workloads dominated by random access on compressible bitvectors at large block size, where the iterative b=63 decoder beat SDSL b=63 on every dataset in the notebook (for example 75 vs 94 ns on WT-WEB-1GB).
Build-time-sensitive pipelines: the notebook shows IT63 construction at 3.2 s vs 21.0 s for SDSL b=63 on WT-DNA-1GB (about 6.5x, derived from page data).
As reference code for the SEA 2025 paper's decoders, to port the iterative or gap-table decoding into your own bitvector.
when_not_to_use: Production use: no LICENSE file (all rights reserved by default), 1 star, no releases, debugging code still present, and hyb_256.hpp is marked broken (its checksums disagree in the notebook).
Rank-heavy workloads on very compressible data: IT63 rank on WT-WEB-1GB was 179 ns vs 148 ns for SDSL b=63, so it is slower there.
When access speed matters more than space: SDSL's rrr_vector<15> (RRR15 row) was fastest overall (110 ns access, 149 ns rank on WT-DNA-1GB) at about 0.90 bits/bit vs 0.71 for IT63.
Incompressible or random dense bitvectors: on RND-1 all H0 variants use more than 1 bit per bit (IT63 1.07), worse than a plain bitvector with rank support.
Non-x86 or pre-BMI2 targets: headers include immintrin.h and select uses _pdep_u64/_pdep_u32 (BMI2).

integration.form: header-only (include/*.hpp), but depends on SDSL headers and library; the benchmark build patches files inside the sdsl-lite submodule
integration.dependencies: sdsl-lite (git submodule; int_vector and bit_vector), Python 3 to generate the de Bruijn headers (dbs15/dbs24/wdbs*.hpp)
integration.min_toolchain: g++ with -std=c++2b (Makefile); h0_gap needs -fconstexpr-ops-limit=5000000000 -fconstexpr-loop-limit=10000000 (GCC-specific flags) for its compile-time tables
integration.platforms: x86-64 with BMI2 (immintrin.h, _pdep_u64); Makefile uses -march=native and reads the cache line size via getconf (Linux)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; query methods are const and the structures are immutable after construction
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — constructed from an sdsl::bit_vector like rrr_vector, but queries are member functions access/rank/select rather than operator[] plus rank_support/select_support objects, and there is no serialization

gotchas: Select timings in the notebook are not valid: the harness (adapted from SDSL's rrr_time_and_space.cpp, which has the same bug) sets stop = timer::now() where it should reset start before the select loop, so every reported select time also includes the rank loop.
The benchmark measures independent random queries (sum of results over 10M queries from 2^20 sampled positions), i.e. throughput-like ns/query, not dependent-query latency.
Each constructor builds four temporary std::vectors copying metadata and block codes (left over from debugging), adding about 8 bytes per 63-bit block of peak memory during construction.

The SDSL baseline is built from patched sdsl_hacks/rrr_vector.hpp and rrr_helper.hpp; the patches add size accessors and an optional RRR_NO_OPT path that the Makefile does not enable, so the baseline appears unmodified in behavior.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over LA-vector or succinct-bitvec-cpp's RRRBitVec only when you specifically need the RRR (block class/offset) representation with faster decoding at b=63; for compressed bitvectors you intend to ship, LA-vector (TALG 2022, select fastest in its comparison) is the better-supported choice, and for uncompressed rank/select SPIDER or rankselect trade more space for speed.
verified_claims_summary: First-party notebook output from a machine labelled 'laptop' (CPU not stated; g++ -std=c++2b -Ofast -march=native) shows the iterative b=63 decoder against SDSL rrr_vector<63> at equal space: access 249 vs 345 ns on WT-DNA-1GB and 75 vs 94 ns on WT-WEB-1GB (about 1.2-1.4x), rank 262 vs 345 ns on DNA but 179 vs 148 ns on WEB (slower); SDSL's rrr_vector<15> remains faster in absolute terms at more space.
status_note: Stale research code (last commit 2025-07-17, 48 commits, 1 star) with no license, so it is reference only: read it for the decoding ideas, do not vendor it.
